name: Queen Anne Playhouse
description: Solid Queen Anne. Front, sides, and roof stay on. The full back, extended up over the attic opening, is the one closure.
concept_note: Approved picture. Not this CAD and not a measured survey.
proportion_note: Assembly is wider than the v4 stack. Turret across the flats is about 148 mm. Porch depth is about 86 mm. Main ridge is below the turret spire.

lighting.architecture: External regulated nominal 5V USB, pre-resistored 5-12V warm-white branches.
lighting.protection_note: No fuse is selected. Do not size one from the 20 mA sum.
lighting.fragile_ornament: Balusters, bargeboard piercings, flower blossoms, and scallop edges are thin. A 0.2 mm nozzle is the ornament setting. They are not claimed durable or safe.

departures_from_concept: The picture is a render, not a survey. The broad front, turret, porch, and street gable follow it. Mouldings are thicker than the render's hairlines.
Play access is the full back, one wall, pulled straight off. The front and both sides stay. The picture's open view is a side cutaway; this house opens at the back.
The back seats 0.45 mm off the jambs. That gap is the fit, not a missing wall. Magnets do not hold the house up. The back is not a brace.
The rear wall's measured bbox fits one print. It is not a 460 mm slab.
Colors in the viewer are the intended palette. One printed part is one material until it is painted.
Balusters, bargeboard piercings, blossoms, and scallop edges are thin. A 0.2 mm nozzle is the ornament setting. They are not claimed durable.
magnet_install_steps: Nominal disc 5.0 x 2.8 mm. Seat 5.6 x 3.2 mm, skin 1.4 mm. Design allowances, not a measured fit.
Hardware is a nominal M2 screw (major 2.0, pitch 0.4, head 3.8 x 1.6) and a nominal M2 hex nut (AF 4.0, thickness 1.6). Those class dimensions are design assumptions, not measurements.
Slide the nut in from the side. The lip in front of it is a 2.5 mm hole, smaller than the nut, so the nut cannot pull out.
Turn the screw in. A 0.12 mm straight pull meets the thread flanks. The seated pair is a clearance fit.
With the strip or retainer on, the side slot is covered. Adult removal: turn the screw out, take the strip or retainer off, then slide the nut out.
Not a tested thread, not a wear test, and not a toy-safety certification.
limits: Unprinted prototype. These STLs are development files, not a finished play kit.

Back screws are drawn as nominal M2x3. The tip is about 0.25 mm past the nut, and the capture strip is still solid at that tip, with about 1.35 mm of plastic beyond it. That clearance was not cut. Bottoming is a risk. Not measured.
Jamb screws are drawn as nominal M2x8. A CAD section put the nut on the screw with about 0.6 mm of empty bore past the tip. That was not a physical test.
Not printed. No strength, tip-over, magnet, or electrical test.
Roofs are gravity seated, not locked. They bear on the fixed shell with the back off.
The back is a closure, not a structural brace. Magnets are not the house's support.
Thin ornament can break. That is not a safety claim.
A 0.2 mm nozzle is a machine some printers can take. It is not confirmed for this house. Nozzle diameter, layer height, and extrusion width are different numbers.

legacy_interface.note: Measured on floor_tile_v0. This house does not use that socket.
